findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed the PIC remade a sanitizer bucket and opened door handles and then proceeded to test sushi acidic levels wearing the same gloves. The PIC was educated during the inspection that after any potential contamination occurs they must remove gloves, wash hands, and put on new gloves before continuing to handle food. Ensure that hands are washed and new gloves are donned after engaging in any activity that can contaminate hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0-10 ppm (quat) when the inspector arrived. During the inspection the bucket was remade and it tested at 200 ppm (quat). Ensure that sanitizing concentrations are always testing at the correct concentration (200-400 ppm for quat).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed the facility has chlorine test strips available but they use quat sanitizer. The inspector explained the importance of using the correct test strips to accurately measure the concentration of sanitizing solutions. The PIC asked the deli manager to use their quat test strips until they are able to purchase the correct type (the sushi station is directly adjacent to the deli). The deli manager agreed and showed the PIC where the test strips are stored. Ensure that there are always test strips available to accurately measure the concentration of sanitizing solutions.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed operator using a wiping cloth which had been sitting on the top counter of the prep cooler during food preparation. The wiping cloth was used to wipe hands and knives during use. The wiping cloth was then brought over to the triple sink where it was rinsed off. Following rinsing, operator folded the wiping cloth and began wiping off food-contact and non-food-contact surfaces on and along the prep cooler including knives and cutting boards. Inspector tested the water on the wiping cloth and ther was zero concentration of sanitizer in the wiping cloth following rinsing and thus no sanitizer used in wiping off food-contact surfaces such as the cutting boards and knives. Inspector had a detailed discussion with operator to educate on proper use of wiping cloths. Wet wiping cloth must be placed in sanitizer solution between each use and may not be allowed to sit on surfaces such as counter tops. If rinsed, wiping cloths must be returned to the sanitizer bucket prior to using the wiping cloths to wipe down food-contact surfaces. Operator stated understanding of this requirement and wiping cloth was immediately placed in the sanitizer bucket with a quaternary ammonium concentration of approximately 200 ppm per inspector test strips. Corrected on site. 

4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: 6-501.12: (A) Observed caulk around window of prep cooler to have mold present. Remove moldy caulk and recaulk around window. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket observed with 0ppm quat. CORRECTED— PIC dumped sanitizer and created a new bucket from the wall mounted dispenser. Concentration observed to be 200ppm.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have concentration based on label (200-400 ppm). [P]
